first:pt-[1px]"><div class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert w-full break-words light markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="42">That’s a great starting point, Danish 👍</p>
<p data-start="44" data-end="356">Your proposed FYP title <strong data-start="68" data-end="156">“Facial Emotion Recognition System for Mental Health Monitoring using Deep Learning”</strong> is actually <strong data-start="169" data-end="200">a strong and relevant title</strong> — especially for BITI (Artificial Intelligence) — because it combines <strong data-start="271" data-end="314">AI, emotion recognition, and healthcare</strong>, which are all trending research areas.</p>
<p data-start="358" data-end="465">Here’s a breakdown to help you move forward step-by-step (since you’re in Week 4 and starting from zero):</p>
<hr data-start="467" data-end="470">
<h3 data-start="472" data-end="519">🧠 Step 1: Validate and refine your title</h3>
<p data-start="520" data-end="865">Your current title is good. But it can be slightly refined for clarity and academic tone:<br>
<strong data-start="610" data-end="623">Option A:</strong> Facial Emotion Recognition System for Mental Health Monitoring using Deep Learning<br data-start="706" data-end="709">
<strong data-start="709" data-end="722">Option B:</strong> Deep Learning-based Facial Emotion Recognition for Mental Health Monitoring<br data-start="798" data-end="801">
✅ This version (B) is shorter and fits UTeM’s preferred style.</p>
<hr data-start="867" data-end="870">
<h3 data-start="872" data-end="943">🗂 Step 2: Understand your report structure (BITI – Product Type)</h3>
<p data-start="944" data-end="1124">Based on the <strong data-start="957" data-end="978">FYP Writing Guide</strong> and the <strong data-start="987" data-end="1011">2025 Report Template</strong>, your <ol data-start="1126" data-end="2150">
<li data-start="1126" data-end="1262">
<p data-start="1129" data-end="1159"><strong data-start="1129" data-end="1157">CHAPTER 1 – Introduction</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1163" data-end="1262">
<li data-start="1163" data-end="1186">
<p data-start="1165" data-end="1186">Background of study</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1190" data-end="1211">
<p data-start="1192" data-end="1211">Problem statement</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1215" data-end="1229">
<p data-start="1217" data-end="1229">Objectives</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1233" data-end="1242">
<p data-start="1235" data-end="1242">Scope</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1246" data-end="1262">
<p data-start="1248" data-end="1262">Significance</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1264" data-end="1552">
<p data-start="1267" data-end="1324"><strong data-start="1267" data-end="1322">CHAPTER 2 – Literature Review &amp; Project Methodology</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1328" data-end="1552">
<li data-start="1328" data-end="1412">
<p data-start="1330" data-end="1412">Review related works (emotion recognition, deep learning, mental health systems)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1416" data-end="1475">
<p data-start="1418" data-end="1475">Discuss algorithms (CNN, FER2013 dataset, OpenCV, etc.)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1479" data-end="1552">
<p data-start="1481" data-end="1552">Explain your methodology (data collection, preprocessing, model design)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1554" data-end="1715">
<p data-start="1557" data-end="1583"><strong data-start="1557" data-end="1581">CHAPTER 3 – Analysis</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1587" data-end="1715">
<li data-start="1587" data-end="1630">
<p data-start="1589" data-end="1630">System requirements (hardware/software)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1634" data-end="1678">
<p data-start="1636" data-end="1678">Functional &amp; non-functional requirements</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1682" data-end="1715">
<p data-start="1684" data-end="1715">Use case diagram, system flow</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1717" data-end="1850">
<p data-start="1720" data-end="1765"><strong data-start="1720" data-end="1763">CHAPTER 4 – Design / Proposed Technique</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1769" data-end="1850">
<li data-start="1769" data-end="1793">
<p data-start="1771" data-end="1793">Architecture diagram</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1797" data-end="1830">
<p data-start="1799" data-end="1830">Deep learning model structure</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1834" data-end="1850">
<p data-start="1836" data-end="1850">Dataset flow</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1852" data-end="1960">
<p data-start="1855" data-end="1887"><strong data-start="1855" data-end="1885">CHAPTER 5 – Implementation</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1891" data-end="1960">
<li data-start="1891" data-end="1936">
<p data-start="1893" data-end="1936">Tools (Python, TensorFlow, Keras, OpenCV)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1940" data-end="1960">
<p data-start="1942" data-end="1960">Code explanation</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="1962" data-end="2072">
<p data-start="1965" data-end="1990"><strong data-start="1965" data-end="1988">CHAPTER 6 – Testing</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1994" data-end="2072">
<li data-start="1994" data-end="2043">
<p data-start="1996" data-end="2043">Model evaluation (accuracy, confusion matrix)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2047" data-end="2072">
<p data-start="2049" data-end="2072">System usability test</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2074" data-end="2150">
<p data-start="2077" data-end="2105"><strong data-start="2077" data-end="2103">CHAPTER 7 – Conclusion</strong></p>
<ul data-start="2109" data-end="2150">
<li data-start="2109" data-end="2131">
<p data-start="2111" data-end="2131">Summary of results</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2135" data-end="2150">
<p data-start="2137" data-end="2150">Future work</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<hr data-start="2152" data-end="2155">
<h3 data-start="2157" data-end="2225">🧾 Step 3: Start writing your <strong data-start="2191" data-end="2219">Chapter 1 (Introduction)</strong> now</h3>
<p data-start="2226" data-end="2275">You can start filling this in even before coding.</p>
<p data-start="2277" data-end="2441">I can help you write <strong data-start="2298" data-end="2311">Chapter 1</strong> right now based on your title, using the official FYP structure and the formatting from the <code data-start="2404" data-end="2440">5-FYP Report Template 2025_v1.docx</code>.</p>

first:pt-[1px]"><div class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert w-full break-words light markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="21">Excellent choice 👍</p>
<p data-start="23" data-end="208">✅ <strong data-start="25" data-end="106">“Deep Learning-Based Facial Emotion Recognition for Mental Health Monitoring”</strong><br data-start="106" data-end="109">
is indeed <strong data-start="119" data-end="146">the most suitable title</strong> — it fits UTeM’s preferred style for BITI projects because:</p>
<ul data-start="209" data-end="425">
<li data-start="209" data-end="274">
<p data-start="211" data-end="274">It starts with the <strong data-start="230" data-end="248">core technique</strong> (“Deep Learning-Based”)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="275" data-end="342">
<p data-start="277" data-end="342">It describes the <strong data-start="294" data-end="309">main system</strong> (“Facial Emotion Recognition”)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="343" data-end="425">
<p data-start="345" data-end="425">It clearly states the <strong data-start="367" data-end="390">purpose/application</strong> (“for Mental Health Monitoring”)</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p data-start="427" data-end="516">So yes, this is the one you should officially use in your report, proposal, and system.</p>
<p data-start="518" data-end="581">Now, before I generate your report draft — do you want me to:</p>
<ol data-start="582" data-end="909" data-is-last-node="" data-is-only-node="">
<li data-start="582" data-end="718">
<p data-start="585" data-end="718"><strong data-start="585" data-end="630">Make the full FYP skeleton (Chapters 1–7)</strong> in short editable form (each section with brief content, ready to expand later),<br data-start="711" data-end="714">
or</p>
</li>
<li data-start="719" data-end="909" data-is-last-node="">
<p data-start="722" data-end="909" data-is-last-node=""><strong data-start="722" data-end="764">Focus only on Chapter 1 (Introduction)</strong> first — with detailed, high-quality writing (background, problem statement, objectives, etc.) so you can submit it to your supervisor next week?</p>
</li>
</ol></div></div></div></div><div class="z-0 flex min-h-[46px] justify-start"><div class="touch:-me-2 touch:-ms-3.5 -ms-2.5 -me-1 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-y-4 p-1 select-none guide).</p>
<p data-start="144" data-end="203">Here’s your <strong data-start="156" data-end="184">complete Chapter 1 draft</strong> for the project:</p>
<blockquote data-start="204" data-end="294">
<p data-start="206" data-end="294"><strong data-start="206" data-end="216">Title:</strong> <em data-start="217" data-end="294">Deep Learning-Based Facial Emotion Recognition for Mental Health Monitoring</em></p>
</blockquote>
<hr data-start="296" data-end="299">
<h2 data-start="301" data-end="331"><strong data-start="304" data-end="331">CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCTION</strong></h2>
<h3 data-start="333" data-end="368"><strong data-start="337" data-end="368">1.1 Background of the Study</strong></h3>
<p data-start="370" data-end="794">Mental health has become an increasing concern in modern society, affecting millions of individuals worldwide. Conditions such as depression, anxiety, and stress often go unnoticed until they reach a severe stage. Traditionally, mental health assessment relies on self-report questionnaires or direct consultation with psychologists. However, these methods can be subjective and require active participation from patients.</p>
<p data-start="796" data-end="1125">In recent years, <strong data-start="813" data-end="849">facial emotion recognition (FER)</strong> has emerged as an important area in artificial intelligence (AI), capable of detecting human emotions based on facial expressions. This capability can support <strong data-start="1009" data-end="1045">mental health monitoring systems</strong>, providing objective and continuous insights into a person’s emotional state.</p>
<p data-start="1127" data-end="1550">With the advancement of <strong data-start="1151" data-end="1168">deep learning</strong>, especially <strong data-start="1181" data-end="1221">convolutional neural networks (CNNs)</strong>, emotion recognition systems can now achieve high accuracy in real-time applications. Combining these technologies enables the development of a system that can analyze facial expressions from images or video streams and classify them into different emotional categories such as happiness, sadness, anger, surprise, or neutral.</p>
<p data-start="1552" data-end="1895">This project proposes a <strong data-start="1576" data-end="1662">Deep Learning-Based Facial Emotion Recognition System for Mental Health Monitoring</strong>, which aims to automatically detect and analyze facial emotions to support early identification of mental health issues. The system can serve as a digital assistant for therapists or individuals to track emotional changes over time.</p>
<hr data-start="1897" data-end="1900">
<h3 data-start="1902" data-end="1931"><strong data-start="1906" data-end="1931">1.2 Problem Statement</strong></h3>
<p data-start="1933" data-end="2002">Mental health assessment is often hindered by the following issues:</p>
<ol data-start="2004" data-end="2469">
<li data-start="2004" data-end="2162">
<p data-start="2007" data-end="2162"><strong data-start="2007" data-end="2036">Subjectivity in diagnosis</strong> – Traditional assessments depend heavily on self-reporting, which may not always reflect an individual’s true mental state.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2163" data-end="2292">
<p data-start="2166" data-end="2292"><strong data-start="2166" data-end="2191">Limited accessibility</strong> – Many individuals do not seek professional help due to social stigma, cost, or lack of awareness.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2293" data-end="2469">
<p data-start="2296" data-end="2469"><strong data-start="2296" data-end="2338">Absence of continuous monitoring tools</strong> – Existing methods fail to provide real-time emotional monitoring that could alert users to early signs of stress or depression.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="2471" data-end="2799">Therefore, there is a need for an <strong data-start="2505" data-end="2525">automated system</strong> that can <strong data-start="2535" data-end="2575">objectively recognize human emotions</strong> through facial expressions. By applying <strong data-start="2616" data-end="2644">deep learning algorithms</strong>, this project aims to create a system that continuously monitors facial emotions and provides valuable data that could assist in mental health evaluation.</p>
<hr data-start="2801" data-end="2804">
<h3 data-start="2806" data-end="2828"><strong data-start="2810" data-end="2828">1.3 Objectives</strong></h3>
<p data-start="2830" data-end="2878">The objectives of this project are as follows:</p>
<ol data-start="2880" data-end="3198">
<li data-start="2880" data-end="2966">
<p data-start="2883" data-end="2966">To design a <strong data-start="2895" data-end="2932">facial emotion recognition system</strong> using deep learning techniques.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2967" data-end="3070">
<p data-start="2970" data-end="3070">To <strong data-start="2973" data-end="2995">train and evaluate</strong> a deep learning model capable of classifying facial emotions accurately.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3071" data-end="3198">
<p data-start="3074" data-end="3198">To <strong data-start="3077" data-end="3110">integrate emotion recognition</strong> results into a <strong data-start="3126" data-end="3164">mental health monitoring dashboard</strong> for visual tracking and analysis.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<hr data-start="3200" data-end="3203">
<h3 data-start="3205" data-end="3237"><strong data-start="3209" data-end="3237">1.4 Scope of the Project</strong></h3>
<p data-start="3239" data-end="3281">The scope of this project is defined as:</p>
<ul data-start="3283" data-end="3871">
<li data-start="3283" data-end="3401">
<p data-start="3285" data-end="3401">The system focuses on <strong data-start="3307" data-end="3342">basic facial emotion categories</strong> such as happy, sad, angry, surprised, fear, and neutral.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3402" data-end="3512">
<p data-start="3404" data-end="3512">The system will utilize publicly available datasets (e.g., <strong data-start="3463" data-end="3474">FER2013</strong>, <strong data-start="3476" data-end="3483">CK+</strong>) for training and testing.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3513" data-end="3602">
<p data-start="3515" data-end="3602">The model will be implemented using <strong data-start="3551" data-end="3561">Python</strong>, <strong data-start="3563" data-end="3583">TensorFlow/Keras</strong>, and <strong data-start="3589" data-end="3599">OpenCV</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3603" data-end="3738">
<p data-start="3605" data-end="3738">The final prototype will run on a <strong data-start="3639" data-end="3673">desktop or web-based interface</strong> that can capture and classify facial expressions in real-time.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3739" data-end="3871">
<p data-start="3741" data-end="3871">The project does <strong data-start="3758" data-end="3792">not perform clinical diagnosis</strong> but provides emotional insights that could assist mental health professionals.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="3873" data-end="3876">
<h3 data-start="3878" data-end="3917"><strong data-start="3882" data-end="3917">1.5 Significance of the Project</strong></h3>
<p data-start="3919" data-end="4026">This project contributes to both <strong data-start="3952" data-end="3973">academic research</strong> and <strong data-start="3978" data-end="4001">societal well-being</strong> in the following ways:</p>
<ul data-start="4028" data-end="4578">
<li data-start="4028" data-end="4168">
<p data-start="4030" data-end="4168"><strong data-start="4030" data-end="4067">Supports mental health awareness:</strong> By enabling non-invasive emotion monitoring, users can better understand their emotional patterns.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4169" data-end="4289">
<p data-start="4171" data-end="4289"><strong data-start="4171" data-end="4207">Advances deep learning research:</strong> The project demonstrates the application of CNNs for human emotion recognition.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4290" data-end="4437">
<p data-start="4292" data-end="4437"><strong data-start="4292" data-end="4344">Provides a foundation for healthcare innovation:</strong> The developed system can be extended into clinical tools or smart mental health platforms.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4438" data-end="4578">
<p data-start="4440" data-end="4578"><strong data-start="4440" data-end="4471">Encourages early detection:</strong> Early signs of emotional instability can be detected, potentially preventing serious mental health issues.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="4580" data-end="4583">
<h3 data-start="4585" data-end="4613"><strong data-start="4589" data-end="4613">1.6 Report Structure</strong></h3>
<p data-start="4615" data-end="4662">This report is organized into seven chapters:</p>
<ul data-start="4664" data-end="5188">

<p data-start="4666" data-end="4773"><strong data-start="4666" data-end="4679">Chapter 1</strong> introduces the research background, problem statement, objectives, scope, and significance.</p>
</li>

<p data-start="4776" data-end="4857"><strong data-start="4776" data-end="4789">Chapter 2</strong> discusses related studies and the project’s research methodology.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4858" data-end="4917">
<p data-start="4860" data-end="4917"><strong data-start="4860" data-end="4873">Chapter 3</strong> presents system and requirement analysis.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4918" data-end="4989">
<p data-start="4920" data-end="4989"><strong data-start="4920" data-end="4933">Chapter 4</strong> explains the design and proposed system architecture.</p>
</li>

<p data-start="4992" data-end="5043"><strong data-start="4992" data-end="5005">Chapter 5</strong> describes the implementation phase.</p>
</li>

</li>

flex-col gap-1 empty:hidden first:pt-[1px]"><div class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert w-full break-words light markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="183">Perfect — I love that mindset, Danish 👏<br data-start="40" data-end="43">
You want your <strong data-start="57" data-end="70">Chapter 1</strong> to sound <strong data-start="80" data-end="139">human-written, deeply reasoned, and academically mature</strong>, not robotic or generic like an AI draft.</p>
<p data-start="185" data-end="435">Let’s polish your <strong data-start="203" data-end="216">Chapter 1</strong> step-by-step into a <strong data-start="237" data-end="266">top-tier UTeM FYP version</strong>:<br data-start="267" data-end="270">
✅ clear structure<br data-start="287" data-end="290">
✅ academic tone<br data-start="305" data-end="308">
✅ logical flow between paragraphs<br data-start="341" data-end="344">
✅ natural phrasing (so it reads like you wrote it yourself)<br data-start="403" data-end="406">
✅ zero “AI-sounding” filler</p>
<hr data-start="437" data-end="440">
<h2 data-start="442" data-end="475">🎓 <strong data-start="448" data-end="475">CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCTION</strong></h2>
<h3 data-start="477" data-end="512"><strong data-start="481" data-end="512">1.1 Background of the Study</strong></h3>
<p data-start="514" data-end="1111">Mental health issues have become a growing concern in recent years, as depression, anxiety, and stress increasingly affect people of all ages and backgrounds. The World Health Organization (WHO) reports that mental disorders are one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. Despite this, mental health evaluation often depends on subjective methods such as self-reported questionnaires or clinical interviews, which rely heavily on individual honesty and professional interpretation. These approaches can overlook subtle emotional changes that may indicate early stages of mental distress.</p>
<p data-start="1113" data-end="1615">Facial expressions are a key indicator of human emotion and can reveal valuable insights into a person’s psychological state. With the emergence of <strong data-start="1261" data-end="1293">Artificial Intelligence (AI)</strong> and <strong data-start="1298" data-end="1320">Deep Learning (DL)</strong>, it is now possible to automatically detect and analyze emotions through images or video feeds. <strong data-start="1417" data-end="1453">Facial Emotion Recognition (FER)</strong> systems apply image processing and machine learning techniques to identify emotions such as happiness, sadness, anger, fear, and surprise based on facial cues.</p>
<p data-start="1617" data-end="2109">Recent developments in <strong data-start="1640" data-end="1680">Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)</strong> have significantly improved the accuracy of emotion recognition systems, making real-time analysis achievable. This technology can be integrated into a <strong data-start="1833" data-end="1868">mental health monitoring system</strong>, allowing users or healthcare professionals to continuously track emotional patterns. Such systems can assist in identifying emotional instability, providing early alerts that may encourage individuals to seek help before symptoms worsen.</p>
<p data-start="2111" data-end="2425">Therefore, this project aims to develop a <strong data-start="2153" data-end="2239">Deep Learning-Based Facial Emotion Recognition System for Mental Health Monitoring</strong>. The proposed system will detect facial emotions using deep learning models and present the results in a monitoring interface that can support self-awareness and mental health tracking.</p>
<hr data-start="2427" data-end="2430">
<h3 data-start="2432" data-end="2461"><strong data-start="2436" data-end="2461">1.2 Problem Statement</strong></h3>
<p data-start="2463" data-end="2560">Mental health evaluation faces several challenges that limit its effectiveness and accessibility:</p>
<ol data-start="2562" data-end="3113">
<li data-start="2562" data-end="2734">
<p data-start="2565" data-end="2734"><strong data-start="2565" data-end="2596">Subjectivity in assessment:</strong> Traditional psychological assessments depend heavily on self-reports, which are influenced by personal bias, mood, or fear of judgment.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2735" data-end="2925">
<p data-start="2738" data-end="2925"><strong data-start="2738" data-end="2764">Lack of accessibility:</strong> Many individuals, particularly in rural areas, have limited access to professional mental health services or feel reluctant to seek help due to social stigma.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2926" data-end="3113">
<p data-start="2929" data-end="3113"><strong data-start="2929" data-end="2972">Absence of continuous monitoring tools:</strong> Existing methods do not provide a way to continuously monitor emotional changes, resulting in missed opportunities for early intervention.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="3115" data-end="3542">These limitations highlight the need for an <strong data-start="3159" data-end="3195">automated and objective approach</strong> to emotion analysis. By leveraging deep learning for facial emotion recognition, this project seeks to create a system that can monitor emotional patterns over time and potentially provide insights into an individual’s mental well-being. Such a system can complement traditional assessments by offering consistent, data-driven emotional analysis.</p>
<hr data-start="3544" data-end="3547">
<h3 data-start="3549" data-end="3571"><strong data-start="3553" data-end="3571">1.3 Objectives</strong></h3>
<p data-start="3573" data-end="3624">The main objectives of this project are as follows:</p>
<ol data-start="3626" data-end="3941">
<li data-start="3626" data-end="3724">
<p data-start="3629" data-end="3724">To design and develop a <strong data-start="3653" data-end="3690">facial emotion recognition system</strong> using deep learning techniques.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3725" data-end="3815">
<p data-start="3728" data-end="3815">To <strong data-start="3731" data-end="3753">train and evaluate</strong> a CNN model for accurate classification of facial emotions.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3816" data-end="3941">
<p data-start="3819" data-end="3941">To <strong data-start="3822" data-end="3863">integrate emotion recognition results</strong> into a <strong data-start="3871" data-end="3909">mental health monitoring dashboard</strong> for visualization and analysis.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<hr data-start="3943" data-end="3946">
<h3 data-start="3948" data-end="3980"><strong data-start="3952" data-end="3980">1.4 Scope of the Project</strong></h3>
<p data-start="3982" data-end="4031">The scope of this project is outlined as follows:</p>
<ul data-start="4033" data-end="4609">
<li data-start="4033" data-end="4145">
<p data-start="4035" data-end="4145">The system will recognize six basic facial emotions: happiness, sadness, anger, fear, surprise, and neutral.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4146" data-end="4257">
<p data-start="4148" data-end="4257">Publicly available datasets such as <strong data-start="4184" data-end="4195">FER2013</strong> and <strong data-start="4200" data-end="4207">CK+</strong> will be used for model training and validation.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4258" data-end="4349">
<p data-start="4260" data-end="4349">The project will be implemented using <strong data-start="4298" data-end="4308">Python</strong>, <strong data-start="4310" data-end="4330">TensorFlow/Keras</strong>, and <strong data-start="4336" data-end="4346">OpenCV</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4350" data-end="4482">
<p data-start="4352" data-end="4482">The developed prototype will operate through a <strong data-start="4399" data-end="4433">desktop or web-based interface</strong> capable of real-time facial emotion detection.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4483" data-end="4609">
<p data-start="4485" data-end="4609">The system will not diagnose mental illnesses but rather serve as a supportive tool to visualize and track emotional trends.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="4611" data-end="4614">
<h3 data-start="4616" data-end="4655"><strong data-start="4620" data-end="4655">1.5 Significance of the Project</strong></h3>
<p data-start="4657" data-end="4727">This project carries both <strong data-start="4683" data-end="4695">academic</strong> and <strong data-start="4700" data-end="4713">practical</strong> significance:</p>
<ul data-start="4729" data-end="5359">
<li data-start="4729" data-end="4883">
<p data-start="4731" data-end="4883"><strong data-start="4731" data-end="4768">Promotes mental health awareness:</strong> The system encourages users to observe their emotional states regularly, helping to foster early self-awareness.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4884" data-end="5021">
<p data-start="4886" data-end="5021"><strong data-start="4886" data-end="4925">Advances deep learning application:</strong> It demonstrates how CNN models can be applied effectively to human emotion recognition tasks.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5022" data-end="5198">
<p data-start="5024" data-end="5198"><strong data-start="5024" data-end="5059">Supports healthcare innovation:</strong> The project lays the groundwork for integrating AI into mental health monitoring tools, potentially assisting therapists and counselors.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5199" data-end="5359">
<p data-start="5201" data-end="5359"><strong data-start="5201" data-end="5231">Encourages proactive care:</strong> Early emotional pattern detection may help prevent the escalation of mental health conditions by prompting timely intervention.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="5361" data-end="5364">
<h3 data-start="5366" data-end="5394"><strong data-start="5370" data-end="5394">1.6 Report Structure</strong></h3>
<p data-start="5396" data-end="5441">This report is organized into seven chapters:</p>
<ul data-start="5443" data-end="5976">
<li data-start="5443" data-end="5556">
<p data-start="5445" data-end="5556"><strong data-start="5445" data-end="5458">Chapter 1</strong> introduces the background, problem statement, objectives, scope, and significance of the study.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5557" data-end="5639">
<p data-start="5559" data-end="5639"><strong data-start="5559" data-end="5572">Chapter 2</strong> reviews existing studies and explains the project’s methodology.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5640" data-end="5704">
<p data-start="5642" data-end="5704"><strong data-start="5642" data-end="5655">Chapter 3</strong> presents the system requirements and analysis.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5705" data-end="5781">
<p data-start="5707" data-end="5781"><strong data-start="5707" data-end="5720">Chapter 4</strong> details the system design and proposed model architecture.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5782" data-end="5835">
<p data-start="5784" data-end="5835"><strong data-start="5784" data-end="5797">Chapter 5</strong> describes the implementation phase.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5836" data-end="5895">
<p data-start="5838" data-end="5895"><strong data-start="5838" data-end="5851">Chapter 6</strong> discusses testing and evaluation results.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5896" data-end="5976">
<p data-start="5898" data-end="5976"><strong data-start="5898" data-end="5911">Chapter 7</strong> concludes the project and suggests possible future improvements.</p>
</li>
</ul>

light markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="334">Nice — let’s turn that “0 knowledge” into a clear, doable roadmap. I’ll give you a step-by-step plan you can follow <em data-start="116" data-end="127">right now</em>, plus the exact apps, commands and deliverables for each stage. I’ll assume you want a working prototype by the end of the semester and that you’re on Windows (adjust small steps for macOS/Linux if needed).</p>
<hr data-start="336" data-end="339">
<h1 data-start="341" data-end="367">Quick summary (one-line)</h1>
<p data-start="368" data-end="531">Start by: <strong data-start="378" data-end="531">set up your dev environment → collect/inspect datasets → build a simple CNN FER model → evaluate → wrap into a simple UI/dashboard → iterate &amp; write.</strong></p>
<hr data-start="533" data-end="536">
<h2 data-start="538" data-end="586">Tools / apps you’ll use (install these first)</h2>
<ul data-start="587" data-end="1200">
<li data-start="587" data-end="655">
<p data-start="589" data-end="655"><strong data-start="589" data-end="601">Anaconda</strong> (recommended) — easily manages Python environments.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="656" data-end="686">
<p data-start="658" data-end="686"><strong data-start="658" data-end="669">VS Code</strong> — code editor.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="687" data-end="737">
<p data-start="689" data-end="737"><strong data-start="689" data-end="705">Git + GitHub</strong> — version control and backup.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="738" data-end="781">
<p data-start="740" data-end="781"><strong data-start="740" data-end="763">Python 3.10 or 3.11</strong> (via conda env)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="782" data-end="846">
<p data-start="784" data-end="846"><strong data-start="784" data-end="808">Jupyter / JupyterLab</strong> — for experiments &amp; visualizations.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="847" data-end="930">
<p data-start="849" data-end="930"><strong data-start="849" data-end="865">Google Colab</strong> (optional) — if your PC GPU is weak; great for quick training.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="931" data-end="1124">
<p data-start="933" data-end="1124"><strong data-start="933" data-end="946">Libraries</strong>: TensorFlow (or PyTorch if you prefer), Keras (if using TF), OpenCV, NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, matplotlib, seaborn (for plots), Flask or Streamlit (for dashboard/proto UI).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1125" data-end="1200">
<p data-start="1127" data-end="1200"><strong data-start="1127" data-end="1138">Postman</strong> (optional) if you build a REST API; not necessary at first.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="1202" data-end="1205">
<h2 data-start="1207" data-end="1258">Immediate setup (do this TODAY — ~30–60 minutes)</h2>
<ol data-start="1260" data-end="1374">
<li data-start="1260" data-end="1326">
<p data-start="1263" data-end="1326">Install Anaconda: <a data-start="1281" data-end="1305" rel="noopener" target="_new" class="decorated-link" href="https://www.anaconda.com/">https://www.anaconda.com<span aria-hidden="true" class="ms-0.5 inline-block align-middle leading-none"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" data-rtl-flip="" class="block h-[0.75em] w-[0.75em] stroke-current stroke-[0.75]"><path d="M14.3349 13.3301V6.60645L5.47065 15.4707C5.21095 15.7304 4.78895 15.7304 4.52925 15.4707C4.26955 15.211 4.26955 14.789 4.52925 14.5293L13.3935 5.66504H6.66011C6.29284 5.66504 5.99507 5.36727 5.99507 5C5.99507 4.63273 6.29284 4.33496 6.66011 4.33496H14.9999L15.1337 4.34863C15.4369 4.41057 15.665 4.67857 15.665 5V13.3301C15.6649 13.6973 15.3672 13.9951 14.9999 13.9951C14.6327 13.9951 14.335 13.6973 14.3349 13.3301Z"></path></svg></span></a> (download, install).</p>

<hr data-start="2349" data-end="2352">
<h3 data-start="2354" data-end="2444">Week 5 — Literature review + datasets (deliverable: short lit review &amp; dataset folder)</h3>
<ul data-start="2445" data-end="3032">
<li data-start="2445" data-end="2611">
<p data-start="2447" data-end="2611">Find <strong data-start="2452" data-end="2473">3–5 recent papers</strong> on facial emotion recognition and 1–2 on mental-health mapping from emotions (you’ll summarize these in Chapter 2). (Use Google Scholar.)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2612" data-end="2872">
<p data-start="2614" data-end="2658"><strong data-start="2614" data-end="2635">Download datasets</strong>: recommended starters:</p>
<ul data-start="2661" data-end="2872">
<li data-start="2661" data-end="2706">
<p data-start="2663" data-end="2706"><strong data-start="2663" data-end="2674">FER2013</strong> (common benchmark; 7 classes)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2709" data-end="2745">
<p data-start="2711" data-end="2745"><strong data-start="2711" data-end="2718">CK+</strong> (controlled expressions)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2748" data-end="2797">
<p data-start="2750" data-end="2797"><strong data-start="2750" data-end="2763">AffectNet</strong> (bigger, if you want more data)</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2800" data-end="2872">
<p data-start="2802" data-end="2872">Optionally small webcam-captured dataset you make (for later testing).</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2873" data-end="3032">
<p data-start="2875" data-end="3032">Inspect datasets: write a Jupyter notebook to load and visualize images and class distribution.<br>
Deliverable: notebook showing sample images and class counts.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="3034" data-end="3037">
<h3 data-start="3039" data-end="3123">Week 6 — Preprocessing &amp; baseline model (deliverable: baseline model + notebook)</h3>
<ul data-start="3124" data-end="3647">
<li data-start="3124" data-end="3417">
<p data-start="3126" data-end="3146">Preprocessing tasks:</p>
<ul data-start="3149" data-end="3417">
<li data-start="3149" data-end="3231">
<p data-start="3151" data-end="3231">Resize images (e.g., 48×48 or 64×64), grayscale or RGB (FER2013 is grayscale).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3234" data-end="3351">
<p data-start="3236" data-end="3351">Face detection &amp; alignment (use <strong data-start="3268" data-end="3290">OpenCV Haarcascade</strong> or MTCNN for better alignment). Alignment improves accuracy.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3354" data-end="3417">
<p data-start="3356" data-end="3417">Data augmentation: flips, small rotations, brightness jitter.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="3418" data-end="3523">
<p data-start="3420" data-end="3523">Create a <strong data-start="3429" data-end="3445">baseline CNN</strong> (small model) in Keras — train for a few epochs so you have working pipeline.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3524" data-end="3647">
<p data-start="3526" data-end="3647">Save model weights and training history.<br>
Deliverable: Notebook with training logs, saved <code data-start="3615" data-end="3625">model.h5</code>, accuracy/loss plots.</p>
</li>
</ul>

class="whitespace-pre! language-python"><span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">from</span></span><span> tensorflow.keras </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">import</span></span><span> layers, models, optimizers
</span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">def</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-title function_">build_baseline</span></span><span>(</span><span><span class="hljs-params">input_shape=(<span class="hljs-params"><span class="hljs-number">48</span></span></span></span><span>,</span><span><span class="hljs-number">48</span></span><span>,</span><span><span class="hljs-number">1</span></span><span>), num_classes=</span><span><span class="hljs-number">6</span></span><span>):
    model = models.Sequential([
        layers.Conv2D(</span><span><span class="hljs-number">32</span></span><span>,</span><span><span class="hljs-number">3</span></span><span>,activation=</span><span><span class="hljs-string">'relu'</span></span><span>,input_shape=input_shape),
        layers.BatchNormalization(), layers.MaxPool2D(),
        layers.Conv2D(</span><span><span class="hljs-number">64</span></span><span>,</span><span><span class="hljs-number">3</span></span><span>,activation=</span><span><span class="hljs-string">'relu'</span></span><span>),
        layers.BatchNormalization(), layers.MaxPool2D(),
        layers.Conv2D(</span><span><span class="hljs-number">128</span></span><span>,</span><span><span class="hljs-number">3</span></span><span>,activation=</span><span><span class="hljs-string">'relu'</span></span><span>),
        layers.BatchNormalization(), layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D(),
        layers.Dense(</span><span><span class="hljs-number">128</span></span><span>, activation=</span><span><span class="hljs-string">'relu'</span></span><span>),
        layers.Dropout(</span><span><span class="hljs-number">0.4</span></span><span>),
        layers.Dense(num_classes, activation=</span><span><span class="hljs-string">'softmax'</span></span><span>)
    ])
    model.</span><span><span class="hljs-built_in">compile</span></span><span>(optimizer=optimizers.Adam(</span><span><span class="hljs-number">1e-3</span></span><span>),
                  loss=</span><span><span class="hljs-string">'categorical_crossentropy'</span></span><span>,
                  metrics=[</span><span><span class="hljs-string">'accuracy'</span></span><span>])
    </span><span><span class="hljs-keyword">return</span></span><span> model
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>
<p data-start="4514" data-end="4561">Train a couple epochs to verify pipeline works.</p>
<hr data-start="4563" data-end="4566">
<h3 data-start="4568" data-end="4647">Week 7 — Improve model + evaluation (deliverable: improved model + metrics)</h3>
<ul data-start="4648" data-end="5095">
<li data-start="4648" data-end="4779">
<p data-start="4650" data-end="4779">Try transfer learning (e.g., EfficientNetB0, MobileNetV2) — fine-tune on FER dataset. Transfer learning often improves results.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4780" data-end="4885">
<p data-start="4782" data-end="4885">Use proper evaluation: train/val/test splits, confusion matrix, precision/recall per class, F1 score.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="4886" data-end="5095">
<p data-start="4888" data-end="5095">Create notebooks with plots (accuracy, loss, confusion matrix) and short analysis text.<br>
Deliverable: Model with at least reasonable validation accuracy (depends on dataset; aim for &gt;60% on FER2013 baseline).</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="5097" data-end="5100">
<h3 data-start="5102" data-end="5180">Week 8 — Real-time demo &amp; face pipeline (deliverable: working webcam demo)</h3>
<ul data-start="5181" data-end="5482">
<li data-start="5181" data-end="5330">
<p data-start="5183" data-end="5207">Build a small demo that:</p>
<ul data-start="5210" data-end="5330">
<li data-start="5210" data-end="5246">
<p data-start="5212" data-end="5246">Captures webcam frames (OpenCV).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5249" data-end="5330">
<p data-start="5251" data-end="5330">Detects faces -&gt; preprocess -&gt; model.predict -&gt; show emotion label over face.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="5331" data-end="5482">
<p data-start="5333" data-end="5482">Make it robust: smoothing/prediction averaging to reduce flicker.<br>
Deliverable: <code data-start="5412" data-end="5428">demo_webcam.py</code> that runs locally and shows predictions in real time.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="5484" data-end="5487">
<h3 data-start="5489" data-end="5564">Week 9 — Mental-health monitoring dashboard (deliverable: prototype UI)</h3>
<ul data-start="5565" data-end="5976">
<li data-start="5565" data-end="5729">
<p data-start="5567" data-end="5617">Build a simple dashboard to log emotion over time:</p>
<ul data-start="5620" data-end="5729">
<li data-start="5620" data-end="5673">
<p data-start="5622" data-end="5673">Option A: <strong data-start="5632" data-end="5645">Streamlit</strong> — easiest for prototypes.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5676" data-end="5729">
<p data-start="5678" data-end="5729">Option B: Flask + simple HTML/JS if you prefer web.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="5730" data-end="5976">
<p data-start="5732" data-end="5751">Dashboard features:</p>
<ul data-start="5754" data-end="5976">
<li data-start="5754" data-end="5776">
<p data-start="5756" data-end="5776">Live feed + label.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5779" data-end="5850">
<p data-start="5781" data-end="5850">Time-series chart of emotions (counts or percentages per day/hour).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="5853" data-end="5976">
<p data-start="5855" data-end="5976">Basic summary/alerts (e.g., if prolonged sadness &gt; X minutes/day).<br>
Deliverable: Streamlit app <code data-start="5949" data-end="5957">app.py</code> that runs locally.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="5978" data-end="5981">
<h3 data-start="5983" data-end="6057">Week 10 — Testing, user study &amp; evaluation (deliverable: test results)</h3>
<ul data-start="6058" data-end="6343">
<li data-start="6058" data-end="6148">
<p data-start="6060" data-end="6148">Test on: unseen video, a few volunteers (ask friends), or your own webcam across days.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6149" data-end="6228">
<p data-start="6151" data-end="6228">Record metrics: detection reliability, latency (ms/frame), false positives.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6229" data-end="6343">
<p data-start="6231" data-end="6343">Prepare test cases and document results for Chapter 6.<br>
Deliverable: Short test report + sample logs/screenshots.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="6345" data-end="6348">
<h3 data-start="6350" data-end="6417">Week 11 — Write Chapters 3–6 drafts (deliverable: report draft)</h3>
<ul data-start="6418" data-end="6683">
<li data-start="6418" data-end="6605">
<p data-start="6420" data-end="6605">Write Methodology (how you trained, datasets, preprocessing), Analysis, Design (architecture), Implementation &amp; Testing chapters using your collected artifacts (notebooks, model, demo).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="6606" data-end="6683">

</li>
</ul>

<h2 data-start="7018" data-end="7052">Practical tips &amp; best practices</h2>
<ul data-start="7053" data-end="7565">
<li data-start="7053" data-end="7121">
<p data-start="7055" data-end="7121"><strong data-start="7055" data-end="7086">Commit early, commit often.</strong> Use descriptive commit messages.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7122" data-end="7192">
<p data-start="7124" data-end="7192"><strong data-start="7124" data-end="7148">Keep small notebooks</strong> (one per experiment) and log hyperparams.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7193" data-end="7327">
<p data-start="7195" data-end="7327"><strong data-start="7195" data-end="7232">Name datasets and scripts clearly</strong> (<code data-start="7234" data-end="7244">data/raw</code>, <code data-start="7246" data-end="7262">data/processed</code>, <code data-start="7264" data-end="7297">notebooks/01-data-inspect.ipynb</code>, <code data-start="7299" data-end="7323">models/fer_baseline.h5</code>).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7328" data-end="7376">
<p data-start="7330" data-end="7376"><strong data-start="7330" data-end="7340">Backup</strong> to GitHub and Google Drive/Colab.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7377" data-end="7457">
<p data-start="7379" data-end="7457"><strong data-start="7379" data-end="7402">Document everything</strong> in README — supervisors like to see methodical work.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="7458" data-end="7565">
<p data-start="7460" data-end="7565"><strong data-start="7460" data-end="7480">Ethics &amp; privacy</strong>: add a short section about data privacy; if you collect people’s faces, get consent.</p>
</li>
</ul>

Let’s go <strong data-start="62" data-end="84">slowly and clearly</strong>, step-by-step, with <em data-start="105" data-end="123">zero assumptions</em> so you can follow even if this is your first time using Git or VS Code.</p>
<hr data-start="199" data-end="202">
<h2 data-start="204" data-end="214">💻 GOAL</h2>
<p data-start="215" data-end="227">You want to:</p>
<ol data-start="228" data-end="371">
<li data-start="228" data-end="261">
<p data-start="231" data-end="261">Open your project in VS Code</p>
</li>
<li data-start="262" data-end="277">
<p data-start="265" data-end="277">Set up Git</p>
</li>
<li data-start="278" data-end="303">
<p data-start="281" data-end="303">Connect it to GitHub</p>
</li>
<li data-start="304" data-end="371">
<p data-start="307" data-end="371">Upload your files (like your Chapter 1, notebooks, code, etc.)</p>
</li>
</ol>
<hr data-start="373" data-end="376">
<h2 data-start="378" data-end="402">🪜 STEP-BY-STEP GUIDE</h2>
<h3 data-start="404" data-end="434">🧩 Step 1: Install VS Code</h3>
<ol data-start="435" data-end="698">
<li data-start="435" data-end="511">
<p data-start="438" data-end="511">Go to 👉 <a data-start="447" data-end="509" rel="noopener" target="_new" class="decorated-link" href="https://code.visualstudio.com/">https://code.visualstudio.com<span aria-hidden="true" class="ms-0.5 inline-block align-middle leading-none"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" data-rtl-flip="" class="block h-[0.75em] w-[0.75em] stroke-current stroke-[0.75]"><path d="M14.3349 13.3301V6.60645L5.47065 15.4707C5.21095 15.7304 4.78895 15.7304 4.52925 15.4707C4.26955 15.211 4.26955 14.789 4.52925 14.5293L13.3935 5.66504H6.66011C6.29284 5.66504 5.99507 5.36727 5.99507 5C5.99507 4.63273 6.29284 4.33496 6.66011 4.33496H14.9999L15.1337 4.34863C15.4369 4.41057 15.665 4.67857 15.665 5V13.3301C15.6649 13.6973 15.3672 13.9951 14.9999 13.9951C14.6327 13.9951 14.335 13.6973 14.3349 13.3301Z"></path></svg></span></a></p>
</li>
<li data-start="512" data-end="560">
<p data-start="515" data-end="560">Click <strong data-start="521" data-end="545">Download for Windows</strong> and install.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="561" data-end="698">
<p data-start="564" data-end="601">During installation, check the boxes:</p>
<ul data-start="605" data-end="698">
<li data-start="605" data-end="638">
<p data-start="607" data-end="638">✅ “Add to PATH (recommended)”</p>
</li>
<li data-start="642" data-end="698">
<p data-start="644" data-end="698">✅ “Register Code as editor for supported file types”</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<hr data-start="700" data-end="703">
<h3 data-start="705" data-end="731">🧩 Step 2: Install Git</h3>
<ol data-start="732" data-end="917">
<li data-start="732" data-end="808">
<p data-start="735" data-end="808">Go to 👉 <a data-start="744" data-end="806" rel="noopener" target="_new" class="decorated-link" href="https://git-scm.com/downloads">https://git-scm.com/downloads<span aria-hidden="true" class="ms-0.5 inline-block align-middle leading-none"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" data-rtl-flip="" class="block h-[0.75em] w-[0.75em] stroke-current stroke-[0.75]"><path d="M14.3349 13.3301V6.60645L5.47065 15.4707C5.21095 15.7304 4.78895 15.7304 4.52925 15.4707C4.26955 15.211 4.26955 14.789 4.52925 14.5293L13.3935 5.66504H6.66011C6.29284 5.66504 5.99507 5.36727 5.99507 5C5.99507 4.63273 6.29284 4.33496 6.66011 4.33496H14.9999L15.1337 4.34863C15.4369 4.41057 15.665 4.67857 15.665 5V13.3301C15.6649 13.6973 15.3672 13.9951 14.9999 13.9951C14.6327 13.9951 14.335 13.6973 14.3349 13.3301Z"></path></svg></span></a></p>
</li>
<li data-start="809" data-end="855">
<p data-start="812" data-end="855">Download and install <strong data-start="833" data-end="852">Git for Windows</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="856" data-end="917">
<p data-start="859" data-end="917">During setup, keep all defaults (don’t change anything).</p>
</li>
</ol>

<h3 data-start="915" data-end="959">🧩 Step 4 — Authentication (if prompted)</h3>
<p data-start="960" data-end="974">Git might say:</p>
<blockquote data-start="975" data-end="1026">
<p data-start="977" data-end="1026">“please complete authentication in your browser…”</p>
</blockquote>
<p data-start="1028" data-end="1172">That’s good 👍 — a GitHub login window will pop up in your browser.<br data-start="1095" data-end="1098">
Just <strong data-start="1103" data-end="1113">log in</strong>, and Git will save the authentication for future pushes.</p>
<p data-start="1174" data-end="1229">After you log in successfully, it’ll upload your files.</p>

class="whitespace-pre! language-markdown"><span><span><span class="hljs-section"># Deep Learning-Based Facial Emotion Recognition for Mental Health Monitoring</span></span><span>

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 👋 Overview</span></span><span>
This project aims to develop a </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) system**</span></span><span> that uses </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Deep Learning**</span></span><span> techniques to monitor emotional states as an indicator for mental health tracking.  
The system detects facial expressions from images or live video feeds and classifies them into basic emotion categories such as </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Happy, Sad, Angry, Fear, Surprise,**</span></span><span> and </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Neutral**</span></span><span>.  
By analyzing these emotions over time, the system can support mental health awareness and early detection of emotional distress.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 🎯 Objectives</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">1.</span></span><span> To design and develop a </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**facial emotion recognition system**</span></span><span> using deep learning.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">2.</span></span><span> To </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**train and evaluate**</span></span><span> a CNN model for emotion classification.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">3.</span></span><span> To integrate the model into a </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**real-time monitoring interface**</span></span><span> for emotion tracking.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 🧠 Methodology Overview</span></span><span>
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">1.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Data Collection**</span></span><span> – Using public datasets such as FER2013 and CK+.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">2.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Data Preprocessing**</span></span><span> – Face detection, resizing, and augmentation using OpenCV and Keras.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">3.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Model Development**</span></span><span> – CNN or Transfer Learning models (e.g., MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB0).
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">4.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**System Integration**</span></span><span> – Real-time emotion prediction via webcam using Python &amp; OpenCV.
</span><span><span class="hljs-bullet">5.</span></span><span> </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Dashboard Development**</span></span><span> – Visualization of emotion history for potential mental health insights.

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## ⚙️ Tools &amp; Technologies</span></span><span>
| Category | Tools / Libraries |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Programming Language | Python 3.10 |
| Deep Learning | TensorFlow, Keras |
| Computer Vision | OpenCV |
| Data Handling | NumPy, Pandas |
| Visualization | Matplotlib, Seaborn |
| Deployment | Streamlit / Flask |
| Version Control | Git &amp; GitHub |
| Environment | Anaconda, VS Code |

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 📆 Weekly Progress Plan</span></span><span>

| Week | Task | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Week 4**</span></span><span> | Setup | Finalized title, set up GitHub, VS Code, and environment. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Week 5**</span></span><span> | Literature Review &amp; Dataset | Research FER &amp; mental health papers, download datasets (FER2013, CK+). |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Week 6**</span></span><span> | Preprocessing &amp; Baseline Model | Implement face detection, data augmentation, build simple CNN. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Week 7**</span></span><span> | Model Optimization | Try transfer learning, tune parameters, evaluate accuracy. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Week 8**</span></span><span> | Real-Time Implementation | Build webcam-based live emotion recognition demo. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Week 9**</span></span><span> | Dashboard Development | Integrate with Streamlit/Flask dashboard for visualization. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Week 10**</span></span><span> | Testing &amp; Evaluation | Conduct tests with new data, analyze confusion matrix, model accuracy. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Week 11**</span></span><span> | Documentation | Write Chapter 2–6, finalize report content. |
| </span><span><span class="hljs-strong">**Week 12**</span></span><span> | Presentation &amp; Submission | Prepare final report, presentation slides, and upload deliverables. |

---

</span><span><span class="hljs-section">## 📁 Repository Structure</span></span><span>
</span></span></code></div></div></pre>

flex-col gap-1 empty:hidden first:pt-[1px]"><div class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert w-full break-words light markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="229">Excellent question, Danish 👏 — and it’s <em data-start="41" data-end="47">very</em> smart that you’re thinking ahead about this now, because this is one of the most common FYP headaches when people start coding on one device and later need to continue on another.</p>
<p data-start="231" data-end="502">✅ <strong data-start="233" data-end="247">Good news:</strong> yes, you can <strong data-start="261" data-end="287">easily move everything</strong> from your PC to your laptop — and I’ll show you the safest, cleanest way to do it.<br data-start="370" data-end="373">
There are <em data-start="383" data-end="388">two</em> main options (GitHub way &amp; manual backup way). I’ll explain both and recommend which to use for your situation.</p>
<hr data-start="504" data-end="507">
<h2 data-start="509" data-end="566">🧩 Option 1 — The Right Way (via GitHub ✅ Recommended)</h2>
<p data-start="568" data-end="727">Since you already have a GitHub repo set up, you don’t even need to copy anything manually.<br data-start="659" data-end="662">
GitHub <strong data-start="669" data-end="706">automatically becomes your bridge</strong> between PC ↔ Laptop.</p>
<h3 data-start="729" data-end="769">🔹 Steps (once only on your laptop):</h3>
<ol data-start="770" data-end="1743">
<li data-start="770" data-end="842">
<p data-start="773" data-end="842">Install <strong data-start="781" data-end="788">Git</strong>, <strong data-start="790" data-end="801">VS Code</strong>, <strong data-start="803" data-end="815">Anaconda</strong> (same setup as your PC).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="843" data-end="913">
<p data-start="846" data-end="913">Open VS Code → open a folder where you want your project to live.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="914" data-end="1122">
<p data-start="917" data-end="946">In the VS Code terminal, run:</p>

<p data-start="1745" data-end="1768">✅ <strong data-start="1747" data-end="1768">Why this is best:</strong></p>
<ul data-start="1769" data-end="1896">
<li data-start="1769" data-end="1798">
<p data-start="1771" data-end="1798">No risk of missing files.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="1799" data-end="1828">

</li>
<li data-start="1829" data-end="1896">
<p data-start="1831" data-end="1896">You can work from any device — even your SV’s lab PC if needed.</p>
</li>
</ul>

</li>
<li data-start="2148" data-end="2204">
<p data-start="2151" data-end="2204">Zip it (<code data-start="2159" data-end="2202">Right-click → Send to → Compressed folder</code>).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2205" data-end="2309">
<p data-start="2208" data-end="2235">Move it to your laptop via:</p>
<ul data-start="2239" data-end="2309">
<li data-start="2239" data-end="2252">
<p data-start="2241" data-end="2252">USB drive</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2256" data-end="2283">
<p data-start="2258" data-end="2283">Google Drive / OneDrive</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2287" data-end="2309">
<p data-start="2289" data-end="2309">AirDrop (if macOS)</p>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-start="2310" data-end="2339">
<p data-start="2313" data-end="2339">Unzip it on your laptop.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="2341" data-end="2423">Then just create the same Anaconda environment there and run your scripts again.</p>
<p data-start="2425" data-end="2445">✅ Works fine, but:</p>
<ul data-start="2446" data-end="2591">
<li data-start="2446" data-end="2511">
<p data-start="2448" data-end="2511">You must remember to always copy the latest version manually.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2512" data-end="2591">
<p data-start="2514" data-end="2591">You might forget to move a new dataset or file.<br data-start="2561" data-end="2564">
That’s why GitHub is safer.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr data-start="2593" data-end="2596">
<h2 data-start="2598" data-end="2660">🧠 Bonus Tip — Keep big files (like datasets) out of GitHub</h2>
<p data-start="2661" data-end="2705">GitHub limits files &gt;100MB. So for datasets:</p>
<ul data-start="2706" data-end="2885">
<li data-start="2706" data-end="2768">
<p data-start="2708" data-end="2768">Store them locally on both devices in a <code data-start="2748" data-end="2755">data/</code> folder, or</p>
</li>
<li data-start="2769" data-end="2885">
<p data-start="2771" data-end="2832">Upload to <strong data-start="2781" data-end="2797">Google Drive</strong>, and in your code use a path like:</p>

<hr data-start="2887" data-end="2890">
<h2 data-start="2892" data-end="2922">💡 Recommended Hybrid Setup</h2>
<p data-start="2923" data-end="2956">Here’s what I’d do if I were you:</p>
<ol data-start="2957" data-end="3219">
<li data-start="2957" data-end="3016">
<p data-start="2960" data-end="3016">Keep <strong data-start="2965" data-end="3003">all source code + docs + notebooks</strong> in GitHub.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3017" data-end="3085">
<p data-start="3020" data-end="3085">Keep <strong data-start="3025" data-end="3054">datasets + trained models</strong> in Google Drive or OneDrive.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3086" data-end="3143">
<p data-start="3089" data-end="3143">Use your <strong data-start="3098" data-end="3123">PC for heavy training</strong> (faster GPU/CPU).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="3144" data-end="3219">
<p data-start="3147" data-end="3219">Use your <strong data-start="3156" data-end="3203">laptop for demo, presentation, and meetings</strong> with your SV.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p data-start="3221" data-end="3322">That way, your supervisor can see live progress on your laptop, while your PC does the heavy lifting.</p>

# Deep Learning-Based Facial Emotion Recognition for Mental Health Monitoring

## 👋 Overview
This project aims to develop a **Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) system** that uses **Deep Learning** techniques to monitor emotional states as an indicator for mental health tracking.  
The system detects facial expressions from images or live video feeds and classifies them into basic emotion categories such as **Happy, Sad, Angry, Fear, Surprise,** and **Neutral**.  
By analyzing these emotions over time, the system can support mental health awareness and early detection of emotional distress.

---

## 🎯 Objectives
1. To design and develop a **facial emotion recognition system** using deep learning.
2. To **train and evaluate** a CNN model for emotion classification.
3. To integrate the model into a **real-time monitoring interface** for emotion tracking.

---

## 🧠 Methodology Overview
1. **Data Collection** – Using public datasets such as FER2013 and CK+.
2. **Data Preprocessing** – Face detection, resizing, and augmentation using OpenCV and Keras.
3. **Model Development** – CNN or Transfer Learning models (e.g., MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB0).
4. **System Integration** – Real-time emotion prediction via webcam using Python &amp; OpenCV.
5. **Dashboard Development** – Visualization of emotion history for potential mental health insights.

---

## ⚙️ Tools &amp; Technologies
| Category | Tools / Libraries |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Programming Language | Python 3.10 |
| Deep Learning | TensorFlow, Keras |
| Computer Vision | OpenCV |
| Data Handling | NumPy, Pandas |
| Visualization | Matplotlib, Seaborn |
| Deployment | Streamlit / Flask |
| Version Control | Git &amp; GitHub |
| Environment | Anaconda, VS Code |

---

## 📆 Weekly Progress Plan

| Week | Task | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| **Week 4** | Setup | Finalized title, set up GitHub, VS Code, and environment. |
| **Week 5** | Literature Review &amp; Dataset | Research FER &amp; mental health papers, download datasets (FER2013, CK+). |
| **Week 6** | Preprocessing &amp; Baseline Model | Implement face detection, data augmentation, build simple CNN. |
| **Week 7** | Model Optimization | Try transfer learning, tune parameters, evaluate accuracy. |
| **Week 8** | Real-Time Implementation | Build webcam-based live emotion recognition demo. |
| **Week 9** | Dashboard Development | Integrate with Streamlit/Flask dashboard for visualization. |
| **Week 10** | Testing &amp; Evaluation | Conduct tests with new data, analyze confusion matrix, model accuracy. |
| **Week 11** | Documentation | Write Chapter 2–6, finalize report content. |
| **Week 12** | Presentation &amp; Submission | Prepare final report, presentation slides, and upload deliverables. |

---

## 📁 Repository Structure


FYPPROJECT/
│
├── data/ # Dataset folder (FER2013, CK+, etc.)
├── notebooks/ # Jupyter notebooks for training and testing
├── models/ # Saved trained models (.h5 files)
├── src/ # Python scripts (preprocessing, training, dashboard)
├── reports/ # Report documents (Chapter 1–7)
├── README.md # Project overview (this file)
└── requirements.txt # Library dependencies


---

## 💡 Future Enhancements
- Add emotion trend analysis using time-series data.
- Integrate with wearable sensor data for multimodal emotion tracking.
- Develop a mobile version for easier access.

---

✅ Week 4 — Environment setup, Chapter 1 complete, GitHub repository initialized.

dark:prose-invert w-full break-words light markdown-new-styling"><p data-start="0" data-end="174">Nice — I’ll walk you through <em data-start="29" data-end="38">exactly</em> what to click/type in Windows + VS Code so you can add that README, commit it, and push to GitHub. Copy–paste the commands where shown.</p>
<hr data-start="176" data-end="179">
<h2 data-start="181" data-end="247">1) Create the README file in VS Code (GUI method — recommended)</h2>
<ol data-start="248" data-end="583">
<li data-start="248" data-end="327">
<p data-start="251" data-end="327">Open <strong data-start="256" data-end="267">VS Code</strong> and make sure your project folder is open (<code data-start="311" data-end="323">FYPPROJECT</code>).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="328" data-end="433">
<p data-start="331" data-end="433">In the Explorer (left panel) click the <strong data-start="370" data-end="382">New File</strong> icon (or right-click the folder → <strong data-start="417" data-end="429">New File</strong>).</p>
</li>
<li data-start="434" data-end="482">
<p data-start="437" data-end="482">Name the file: <code data-start="452" data-end="463">README.md</code> and press Enter.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="483" data-end="553">
<p data-start="486" data-end="553">Paste the full README content you already have into the new file.</p>
</li>
<li data-start="554" data-end="583">
<p data-start="557" data-end="583">Save the file: <code data-start="572" data-end="582">Ctrl + S</code>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<hr data-start="585" data-end="588">
<h2 data-start="590" data-end="665">2) Stage, commit and push using VS Code terminal (step-by-step commands)</h2>
<ol data-start="666" data-end="1854">
<li data-start="666" data-end="838">
<p data-start="669" data-end="772">Open terminal in VS Code: menu <strong data-start="700" data-end="727">Terminal → New Terminal</strong>.<br data-start="728" data-end="731">
The prompt should show something like:</p>

<li data-start="953" data-end="1013">

<li data-start="1017" data-end="1083">

</li>
<li data-start="1087" data-end="1129">
